1) Thoughts on playing Binko
2) A message for Yurukill: The Calumniation Games players

"Binko... She's multifaceted, that's for sure. I think she's really charming! Is that okay?
"Yeah, why not?" Ah, th-thanks. Binko's with me today, actually. She'll leave you constantly guessing at who the real Binko is, and even then, she's just a really great person. "Thanks." As I was reading through the script for Yurukill: The Calumniation Games, with all its twists and turns and nail-biting developments, I was wondering just how it would end. Erm... "Are you gonna talk about all the unique characters?" Yes, exactly! Thanks, Binko, you're the best. "You leave this to me." Where was I? Yeah, so just like Binko said, the characters are all so unique, they're sure to steal your heart given half the chance. I really hope that players are won over by just how interesting they all are, and get sucked right into the story. How was that, Binko? "Thanks for that. Everyone! I’m waiting to meet you all in the wonderful world of Yurukill!"

notes.title: Yurukill: The Calumniation Games - Introducing: Allan Poe Akechi
notes.content:
Introducing Allan Poe Akechi + A special message from voice actor Tomokazu Sugita!


Allan Poe Akechi
Voice: Tomokazu Sugita
Age: 30 Birthday: January 2 Star sign: Capricorn

Dislikes: Cold cases
Interests: Solving cases

Private detective, alias: Allan Poe Akechi. He claims to be a talented investigator, but his powers of deduction are somewhat questionable. Apparently, he was arrested for peeping during an investigation and claims to be falsely accused. His real name is Benitaro Barahabara.


[previewyoutube=tmj5Ta82oV4;full][/previewyoutube]

Don’t forget to check out Tomokazu Sugita’s comments on playing the role!

[previewyoutube=cP-hg8szbSI;full][/previewyoutube]

1) Thoughts on playing Allan Poe
2) A message for Yurukill: The Calumniation Games players


"Think of that hospital room scene from the Touch manga. (Translator's note: Touch was a popular high school baseball manga written and illustrated by Mitsuru Adachi. Sugita is referring to a famously emotionally-charged scene in which the protagonist is sitting next to the hospital bed his recently deceased younger twin brother is lying in, commenting on how picture perfect he looks, despite having passed on.) Shoot 'em up games aren't supposed to look this good! There are investigation sections, there are shooting sections. What's going on? Why don't you tell me? That's what I want to ask Allan Poe. But, in all seriousness, I'm very hyped for this game. I love shoot 'em ups even though I'm terrible at them. I hope the genre never dies. Oh, and I'm dying to find out just how the investigation sections are linked with the shoot 'em up sections! I tell you, shoot 'em up games aren't supposed to look this good… To everyone planning on playing Yurukill: here are some random "facts". There may even be a chance that something I've said turns out to be true! I'll leave you guys to try and sort the facts from the mumbo jumbo. Okay, here goes. Yu Kobayashi appears as a live action villain in the game. (That sounds kind of believable actually...) All the bullet sounds are her voice, too. Anyway, this game is a fusion of adventure and shoot 'em up, in fact, I've heard it described as a "Zunō Senkan Garu" for the modern generation. (Translator's note: Zunō Senkan Garu was a Japanese top down shoot 'em up released in 1985.) I hear it has RPG elements, too. Oh boy, I'm so excited... What else can I say? Ah, forget it. You'll see what the hype is all about once you play it!"

notes.title: Yurukill: The Calumniation Games - Introducing: Keiichi Oka
notes.content:
Keiichi Oka
Voice: Hiroki Yasumoto
Age: 24 Birthday: November 3 Star sign: Scorpio
Blood type: A
Likes: Hanaka
Dislikes: Meddlesome nerds
Interests: Being a fan

Keiichi is a diehard fan still devoted to Hanaka despite her serving a prison sentence. He is easily excitable when it comes to Hanaka, but gentlemanly, and respectful of the distance between fan and pop star. He is taking part in the Yurukill Games to help Hanaka prove her innocence.

[previewyoutube=NIF5ABjSoI4;full][/previewyoutube]

Don’t forget to check out Hiroki Yasumoto’s comments on playing the role!

[previewyoutube=uuC-te5rCDM;full][/previewyoutube]

1) Thoughts on playing Keiichi
2) A message for Yurukill: The Calumniation Games players

"Keiichi Oka's a fairly intense looking character, and well, let's just say that inside he's even more intense. I suppose this posed a challenge for me when thinking about how to approach his character. My first impression was that he was a bit self-centered and kind of unloveable. But as I read more, I began to realize that, actually, this guy wasn't a completely lost cause. He's irritating, clingy, formidable, but ultimately a decent guy, and I really tried my hardest to convey that with my performance. If players get to the end and think, "this guy's kinda sweet," then that'll be more than enough of a reward for me, and for Oka, himself. By all means, please check out the game! This is an adventure game, but that's not all. This is a hybrid effort. I get the impression some people may find that somewhat of a barrier to entry, but I'd urge them to give it a try. The story in and of itself is a whole lot of fun, and there's also an easy mode. So basically, there's no need to be worried. Also, the characters may all be utterly mad, but those mad characters slot perfectly into a super engaging, well-constructed story that's a treat to dig into. That's why I want as many people as possible to play the game. I completely wore out my throat a bunch of times during the recording, and I'd love for everyone to see the hard work that went into Yurukill!"

Because she's been toiling away on the bottom rungs of the pop star circuit, she's no stranger to hardship as well as the sweeter things in life. She's got plenty of very typical pop star quirks, and there were some difficult scenes where I had to really work to keep up with the changing pace of her emotions. I just hope that on the whole, her dedication, professionalism and cuteness shine through. Simply put, Yurukill: The Calumniation Games has a fascinating story—the kind that shocks and chills you and really gets under your skin, and I mean that in the best possible way. I really hope players get stuck into the quizzes and shoot 'em up sections, get to know all the characters and the incidents they're embroiled in, and get to the bottom of the mystery of Yurukill Land!"

Gentoku is the son of Yurukill, Inc.’s CEO. He feigns being mild-mannered, but inside is malicious, cold-hearted, and abusive. He’s unable to suppress his instinctive “tut” whenever he gets annoyed. He’s taking part in the Yurukill Games as part of a deal with his father.

2) A message for Yurukill: The Calumniation Games players

"Gentoku Omuro looks like the kind of guy who was born with a silver spoon in his mouth, and he has this really refined, gentle way of speaking. But the further into the story you get, you start to see another side of his character—to me that's what's so appealing about him. Just like Gentoku, I think there's a lot lurking beneath the surface of the other characters too, so I hope players enjoy delving into that aspect of the game. Yurukill... it's a hell of a ride, haha. When I first saw the title, I got the feeling it'd be a pretty disturbed story. But then again, you've got the "Games" aspect of the title to consider as well—which really piqued my interest and got me thinking just exactly what kind of game this was. I think ultimately, the main draw of this game is the fact that when you start to unpack it, there's all sorts to dive into. Having done voice work on the game, I can say that everything about it, including the characters, is really distinctive. I hope players leave no stone unturned when they try Yurukill: The Calumniation Games out!"

I bet even Kagura's got all sorts going on in that cheerful, lackadaisical head of hers. Or does she? Maybe she doesn't? Or maybe she does... Haha. If you do a little bit of digging there's plenty underneath the surface. Which I think sums up the game pretty well. Not only is it an exciting new fusion of shoot 'em up action and puzzles that'll have you scratching your head, it's also packed with deep characters brimming with personality. "Futa Yamada is the eldest of two twins. I'm not a twin, so I had to try and envisage his mindset as I was playing him. I guess I came away feeling like being a twin must be pretty cool. The Yamada brothers are caught up in a fairly crazy episode, so I'd love for players to get to the bottom of it. There's a closeness to their relationship that comes from them being twins—it's pretty special, I think! Futa's this real cool, but equally hot-headed character, so there's a real gap between those two traits, and I think that's something players will appreciate. Overall, I had a lot of fun playing Futa! To all the Yurukill players out there... Sometimes in life, we find ourselves falsely accused of something we didn't do. When I was in elementary school, I once picked up a recorder off the floor, only for a girl in my class to accuse me of trying to steal it. I told her she'd got it all wrong... anyway, Yurukill is like that, but dialed up to 11—with the characters trying to clear their names. The story's twists and turns will definitely have you on the edge of your seats, so by all means, please dive in. I mean, I'm also looking forward to playing!"

notes.title: Yurukill: The Calumniation Games - Introducing: Rina Azami
notes.content:
Rina Azami
Voice: Saori Hayami

Age: 17 Birthday: July 22 Star sign: Cancer
Blood type: A
Likes: Her family
Dislikes: Fire
Interests: Keeping a picture diary

Rina is strikingly pretty but has trouble expressing herself, and is brusque and cold to everyone she meets. She often shows extraordinary hatred towards Sengoku. Her reasons for taking part in the Yurukill Games are unknown.

[previewyoutube=XQYuW9Fmhuc;full][/previewyoutube]

Don’t forget to check out Saori Hayami’s comments on playing the role!

[previewyoutube=cRTuwDJTUuA;full][/previewyoutube]

"Rina's tricky to read. The more you uncover about her past and the unfortunate circumstances she finds herself in, the more tragic her character feels. But in the latter half of the game, she has all these lines that help you get a proper sense of what's going on inside her head. I feel like the recording really brought out those subtleties in her character. I had a lot of fun! There are puzzle solving and mystery sections, and then on the other hand you have the shooting parts. The game is definitely packed with all kinds of tasty morsels. The music and visuals are super cool, and above all, the characters have such unique personalities. I hope players get wrapped up in figuring out each character's history and the mysteries surrounding them, and enjoy their time with Yurukill: The Calumniation Games!"

notes.title: Yurukill: The Calumniation Games - Introducing: Sengoku Shunju
notes.content:
Sengoku Shunju
Voice: Takuya Eguchi

Age: 29 Birthday: March 31 Star sign: Aries
Blood type: O
Likes: Iced coffee
Dislikes: Prison
Interests: Board games

Sengoku was imprisoned for a mass murder case in which 21 people burned to death. He is sociable and considerate. He has protested his innocence for over 10 years, and vows to emerge from the Yurukill Games victorious with his teammate, Rina.

[previewyoutube=0m259lW8vco;full][/previewyoutube]

Don’t forget to check out Takuya Eguchi’s comments on playing the role!

[previewyoutube=Qy1jrUWPXR4;full][/previewyoutube]

1) Thoughts on playing Sengoku
2) A message for Yurukill: The Calumniation Games players

"Poor Sengoku, he's got a lot on his plate. He's served 10 years of a 999 year sentence, all on false charges. He starts off being a bit hesitant and reactionary, but he gradually comes into his own and takes the reins—that character arc was something I paid close attention to in my performance. The game is packed with all kinds of different puzzles, and that called for multiple variations in terms of dialogue. The game gives you different choices in different situations, which have an impact on the outcome I mapped out a plan to help me keep track of what kind of takes were appropriate based on the flow of the story, but there were times when certain lines just didn't sound quite right to me, and so I ended up doing a bunch of retakes until I was completely satisfied. All of which to say, I'd love for players to pick all kinds of choices throughout the game when they give it a try."
